input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: The first Section 2.2 imposes full-term exclusive dealing on Customer for hosted analytics services with no category limitation beyond that service line, no 12-month cap, and no automatic exit on service-level or delivery failures — walk-away territory under this rule and a failure of the fallback on every element. It also conflicts with Section 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and Section 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity commitment). We take the preferred position and convert the appointment to non-exclusive rather than negotiating a narrowed exclusivity, which also removes the internal inconsistency.

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.

proposal.summary: Convert the first Section 2.2 from a sole-and-exclusive-provider commitment to a non-exclusive appointment with no Customer exclusivity obligation.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have changed the first Section 2.2 so that Vendor is a non-exclusive provider and Customer carries no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation, consistent with our position and with Sections 2.1 and 12.3. If some exclusivity is essential, we could discuss a narrow arrangement limited to a defined product category for no more than 12 months that ends automatically on any service-level or delivery-date failure.

ops.oldText: will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term
ops.newText: will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services, and Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation
